source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Mechanical V8, p.6-28

procedures.title: Valve mechanism (V8): install and adjust
steps: Hydraulic lifters: from zero clearance, tighten the nut 1 more turn to center the lifter plunger; nothing else is needed.
Hydraulic lifters, No. 1 firing position: adjust exhaust 1, 3, 4, 8 and intake 1, 2, 5, 7.
Hydraulic lifters: turn the crank one revolution until the damper mark and "0" line up again (No. 6 firing) and adjust exhaust 2, 5, 6, 7 and intake 3, 4, 6, 8.
Mechanical lifters: find No. 1 firing position the same way as for hydraulic lifters.
Mechanical lifters, No. 1 firing: set exhaust 4, 8 and intake 2, 7 to spec with a feeler gauge (see figure 4V in the manual).
Turn the crank 1/2 revolution (180°) clockwise and set exhaust 3, 6 and intake 1, 8.
Turn another 180° clockwise until the damper mark and "0" line up again (No. 6 firing) and set exhaust 5, 7 and intake 3, 4.
Turn another 180° clockwise and set exhaust 1, 2 and intake 5, 6.
Re-set mechanical lash hot with the engine running, as described under Engine Tune Up.
Adjust carburetor idle speed and mixture.

procedures.title: Hydraulic valve lifters: locate noisy lifter
steps: Hold one end of a garden hose about 4 feet long near each intake and exhaust valve and the other end to your ear to pinpoint the noisy lifter.
Or rest a finger on each valve spring retainer; a faulty lifter gives a distinct shock as the valve seats.
notes: Hard rapping: plunger stuck tight in the body so the spring cannot return it, from heavy varnish or carbon, or galling from dirt or metal wedged between plunger and body.
Moderate rapping: leakdown rate too high, leaking check valve seat, or wrong adjustment.
Noise through the whole valve train: almost always too little oil or wrong adjustment.
Hydraulic lifters rarely need attention; they need no readjustment, just clean handling when serviced.
